summary: The lower-level accessibility hooks beneath React Aria Components. Apache-2.0, active, React 18/19 compatible, and useful when the component layer is too opinionated. It has the same no-provenance gap and a large install footprint.
reasoning: Active release line: 3.53.1 published 2026-10-09, released with react-aria-components 1.22.1.
Peers React 16.8-19; the component spike exercised this hook layer through React Aria Components.
Provides the accessibility behaviour for custom primitives: focus, press, keyboard, overlays, collections, selection and internationalization.
No install scripts and no recorded OSV advisories.
No npm provenance; pin 3.53.1 exactly and record the gap.
About 58 MB installed with React 19; use it only when the component layer cannot express the needed primitive.
caveats: Large install footprint (about 58 MB with React 19).
React Aria Components already includes this layer; do not add both unless you are writing custom primitives.
Hooks are lower-level and require more accessibility knowledge than the component APIs.
No separate spike for a custom hook-only primitive; the component spike exercised the same runtime.

evidence.label: License
evidence.detail: Apache-2.0; the isolated tree is permissive.

evidence.label: React compatibility
evidence.detail: peerDependencies react/react-dom: ^16.8.0 || ^17.0.0-rc.1 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0-rc.1. The component spike used React 19.2.0.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: 9 runtime dependencies; about 58 MB installed with React 19; 15.4 MB unpacked.

evidence.label: Install scripts
evidence.detail: No preinstall, install or postinstall script in the isolated tree.

evidence.label: npm provenance
evidence.detail: No npm attestation for 3.53.1; published from the Adobe npm account.

evidence.label: Runtime behaviour
evidence.detail: Exercised through react-aria-components 1.22.1 in the dialog spike; the dialog opened with an accessible label and focus inside.
